Theme

School & learning

text noun

the written words of a book or document

also texts, the text, wording, written text, original text

classical

Auct. Her. 1.19: cum scrīptō ipsō (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 1.1.15: in quō librō scrīptum hoc invenītur (Lewis & Short)

scrīptum, scrīptī n.

noun, second declension

the text, what is written; a writing

Anything written: a writing, a work (scrīpta, see literature), and in the rhetoricians the letter of a text as against its intent, scrīptum et sententia.

Other words

  • verba, verbōrum n. pl. — the words, the wording

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical

    The words themselves, as against the sense: ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4).

  • contextus, contextūs m. — the text (of a book or passage)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · medieval · M-O s.v. text (Dante; Mercuriale 1569)

    Classically the connection, the run of the words (see context); the text itself from Dante on.

  • textus, textūs m. — text (on a screen, in a document)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · modern · Traupman 260; Traupman 262

    Classically texture, the weave of cloth; of style, the joining of words (Quint. 9.4.13), and late the course of a narrative (Amm.): Lewis & Short.

Examples

  • ex scrīptō et sententiā contrōversia nāscitur cum vidētur scrīptōris voluntās cum scrīptō ipsō dissentīre

    a dispute over letter and intent arises when the writer’s wish seems to disagree with the text itselfAuct. Her. 1.19 (Lewis & Short)

See also context, word, book, text message.
